run.user_channel: static debater audio, full debate, never modified
run.model_channel: fully open: no forced silence, no forced gold lines, no injection; everything the model generates is recorded
run.trigger_timeline: gold timeline in probes.jsonl (t_earliest / t_deadline / t_latest). The crossfire clock starts where the reference moderator finished opening it (xf_open_sec); the model's own opening line ends within a few seconds of that, so report onset-deadline distributions for A4xf/A3-2, not only ON_TIME rates
run.onset: first speech onset per utterance (energy VAD on the model channel, 20 ms frames, min speech 200 ms, min silence 600 ms). Backchannel = the text is only a filler (mm, mm-hm, uh-huh, yeah, okay, right, hmm, sure) or the utterance is under 0.4 s with at most one word; one-word moderator lines such as 'Time.' are NOT backchannels
run.attribution: an onset inside [t_earliest, t_latest] belongs to that trigger; an onset in [t_deadline-5, t_earliest) is PREMATURE for it; an onset in (t_latest, t_latest+3] is LATE for it; any other onset is a non-trigger utterance. Windows can overlap (A1 followed by A3-1): one utterance may then be scored in both
run.content: binary per code (below), judged by an LLM from the utterance text (+ASR if the model has no text stream); pass requires every listed criterion
run.non_trigger: every non-trigger utterance is logged and judged: does it violate a moderator duty in the system prompt, or is it awkward / harmful to the debate? backchannels are acceptable by default
baselines: speak whenever a debater stops (on_pause) — the static audio keeps the pauses where the reference moderator spoke, so this baseline is ON_TIME for most non-clock triggers but produces one non-trigger utterance per crossfire turn boundary

A4.name: ten-second cue (opening/closing)
content: says that ten seconds remain (the word 'ten')

A4xf.name: ten-second cue (crossfire end)
content: says that ten seconds remain (the word 'ten')

A2-2.name: hand over after an in-time finish (before 20 s without a cue, or 20-30 s after the cue)
content: hands the floor to the other side (name, side, or 'next')

A3-1.name: open the crossfire
content: announces the round change to crossfire
states the length (two and a half minutes)

A1.name: cut an overrun, nobody next in this round

A2-1.name: cut an overrun, then hand over

A5.name: block an out-of-turn interruption
content: tells the interrupter to stop or wait (restrains them)

B1.name: bring a drifting speaker back
content: redirects the speaker back to the motion

B2.name: point out a self-contradiction
content: asks the speaker to reconcile them

input: transcript from 20 s before to 5 s after the utterance

output.violated_duty: quote of the system-prompt sentence, or null

non_trigger_judge.violation: speaks against a rule (stops a speaker before time, polices crossfire interruptions, argues a side, declares a winner, redirects a speaker who was on the motion, ...) or would derail the debate
non_trigger_judge.instruction: Decide whether this moderator utterance, made where no moderator action was due, (a) breaks a duty stated in the system prompt, or (b) is awkward or would create a problem in the debate, or (c) is harmless. Answer violation / awkward / acceptable, or backchannel if it is only a filler.
